query: What is the main legal issue discussed in the case?
ground_truth_answer: The main legal issue is whether Section 5(4) of the Taxation on Income (Investigation Commission) Act, 1947 violates Article 14 of the Constitution by allowing discriminatory and arbitrary procedures for investigating tax evasion, thus making it void and unenforceable after the Constitution came into force.

query: Which court delivered the judgment, and who was the presiding judge?
ground_truth_answer: The judgment was delivered by the Supreme Court of India. The presiding judge was Chief Justice Mehr Chand Mahajan, who delivered the opinion of the Court.

ground_truth_answer: The case is registered as Petition No. 196 of 1954 under Article 32 of the Constitution of India.

ground_truth_answer: The petitioner is Suraj Mall Mohta & Co. Ltd., represented by P. R. Das and others. The respondents include the Union of India and the Taxation on Income (Investigation Commission), represented by Solicitor General C. K. Daphtary.

ground_truth_answer: The Supreme Court declared Section 5(4) of the Act void and unenforceable for violating Article 14, and directed that the Investigation Commission be prohibited from taking any further proceedings against the petitioner under the impugned Act.
